1	# Task 10: Click-to-plant garden that grows over time
2	
3	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, rendering to the canvas with id #app. The app is an interactive 3D garden. A flat ground plane (soil or grass) fills the lower part of the view, with a soft sky or background behind it and a camera looking down at it from an angle so the whole plot is visible.
4	
5	When the user clicks on the ground, a new plant must be planted at the exact spot that was clicked (the click must be mapped to the ground, not just to the screen centre). Each plant starts as a tiny sprout and grows smoothly over about 8 seconds into a mature plant (for example a stem with leaves and a flower or a small bush) that is visibly larger, with a different shape or colour from the sprout. Plants must keep growing independently, so a plant planted later is smaller than one planted earlier. Vary the flower colour or size between plants so a full garden does not look uniform. Support at least 40 plants at once without dropping below a smooth frame rate, and ignore clicks that do not hit the ground.
6	
7	Add a small on-screen DOM overlay in a corner showing the text 'Plants: N' where N is the current plant count, and a 'Clear' button that removes all plants. The scene should have lighting and soft shadows so plants look grounded, and it should render correctly on first load with no console errors and with zero plants planted.
8	
9	Expose a read-only object on window named

content.thinking:
I can't verify type-checking without the package installed, so I'll just assume vertical FOV in degrees and move forward with the code, accepting I can't confirm picking behavior directly. Default directional shadow settings should be fine, and I'm checking how to properly call setInstances on a node through the typed API.

For hidden instances, I'm positioning them far below the scene and scaling them near-zero so they don't cast shadows. I'm designing the plant geometry using unit primitives scaled per-part: stem height grows with an eased growth value up to 1.75, with leaves placed at varying heights and azimuths as flattened, rotated spheres offset outward from the stem.

I'm figuring out sprout visibility at the camera distance — doing a quick pixel-size calculation to make sure a tiny sprout is still a few pixels wide on screen, then bumping up sizes for both sprout and mature plant so they read clearly at 640x360. Now I'm starting on the flower, having it bud in once growth passes 0.55 using a smoothstep-based bud scale centered on the stem.

Working out petal geometry next — using flattened spheres arranged radially around the flower head, scaled by growth factor and overall size, and considering whether the flower should tilt toward the camera given its downward viewing angle (deciding to skip that for now). I'm also mapping out color transitions from light green sprout tones to darker mature greens for the stem and leaves, plus a greenish bud color before the flower opens.

Then I plan the instanced object structure for stems, leaves, petals, and center spheres, scaling counts across up to 120 plants (480 leaves, 720 petals total), and thinking through performance by only rebuilding geometry per-frame while plants are actively growing, keeping static ones cheap.

For timing, I decide to drive growth off a real clock using performance.now() minus the planted timestamp divided by 8000, clamped, rather than accumulating per-frame dt which could be throttled or inconsistent in headless Chromium.

I also plan to expose a read-only __TASK_STATE__ object via a getter on window that lazily builds the plants array, without needing Object.freeze, and I'm starting to think about a fixed-position DOM overlay for displaying state in a corner of the screen.

I settle on positioning the overlay at top-left near the canvas, with the canvas click listener separate so overlay clicks don't trigger planting, and I use clientX/clientY mapped through getBoundingClientRect to normalized coordinates. For bounds checking, I restrict planting to within the visible ground plane and have __plantAt return false for out-of-range coordinates, and I decide to cap the plant count at 150, dropping the oldest when exceeded.

Now I'm working out plant size variation, lighting setup with hemisphere and directional shadows, and color interpolation in HSL space for the stems, along with the typing for the instance transform and color arrays.

For readiness signaling, I need the overlay text to update only when the plant count changes, and I want to make sure the ready flags get set properly after app.ready() resolves and the first frame renders, rather than firing prematurely.

I'll initialize instances with all entries hidden at max capacity and colors set to white as placeholders before populating real data.

I wrote src/main.ts for the click-to-plant garden, but I couldn't run or fully typecheck it. `@aura3d/engine` isn't installed in this sandbox (`node_modules/@aura3d` is empty). The only typecheck error is the unresolved module import. The code follows the API in `llms.txt`.

- **Scene:** a 24×18 grass plane under a light-blue sky background, a perspective camera at [0,16,19] looking at [0,0,1], a hemisphere light, and a shadow-casting directional light.
- **Plants:** four instanced meshes with 150 slots, so the 40+ plants run in a few draw calls. Each plant has a stem, 4 leaves, a bud or flower centre, and 6 petals. Growth is timed from `performance.now()` over 8 seconds with smoothstep easing. A plant starts as a small pale-green sprout, darkens to green, then opens petals in a random hue and size. At 150 plants the oldest is removed.
- **Click mapping:** I compute the click ray from the known camera position, target and field of view, and intersect it with y=0.   - `window.__TASK_STATE__` is a read-only getter with `plantCount`, `plants` and `ready`.
  - `window.__plantAt(x, z)` plants at ground coordinates and returns false if they're off the ground.
